body.p: This communication is responsive to the Office action dated 15 August 2024 as extended, where applicable, under 37 C.F.R. §1.136(a) by payment of appropriate extension of time fees.
Claims 1, 2, 6-11, 13, 16, 18, 24, 27, 32, 36, 38, 40-44 and 48 were pending prior to this communication.
In this communication, the Applicant has amended claims 1, 6, 7, 10, 16, 24, 32, 38, 40, 43 and 48 as set out above.
The Applicant submits that these amendments are completely supported by the application as filed and add no new matter.
Claims 1, 2, 6-11, 13, 16, 18, 24, 27, 32, 36, 38, 40-44 and 48 are pending for consideration.
The Applicant has amended claim 6 to depend from claim 1 and submits that claim 6 (as a result of its amended dependency) is clear and otherwise complies with 35 USC §112.

The Examiner indicated that previously pending claims 7-11, 13, 16, 18, 38 and 40-44 recited allowable subject matter and would be allowed if they were amended to incorporate the features of their respective based claims and any intervening claims.
The Applicant has put these claim into condition for allowance by:
" amending claim 7 to incorporate its base claim (claim 1) and intervening claim 2;
" amending claim 10 to incorporate its base claim (claim 1); " amending claim 16 to incorporate its base claim (claim 1);
" amending claim 38 to incorporate its base claim (claim 32) and intervening claim 36;
" amending claim 40 to incorporate its base claim (claim 32); and
" amending claim 43 to incorporate its base claim (claim 32).
The Applicant submits that as a result of these amendments claims 7, 10, 16, 38, 40 and 43 are in condition for allowance.
Claims 8, 9, 11, 13, 18, 41, 42, and 44 each depend from one of these allowable claims and are submitted to be allowable for at least this reason.

The Examiner has raised A VERTICAL AND HORIZONTAL 3-AXIS HAND-HELD CONFOCAL SCANNER FOR SKIN IMAGING APLICATIONS, April 2015 (Chen) in connection with previously pending claims 1, 2 and 24 and the combination of Chen and US2014/0023993 (Zeng et al.) in connection with previously pending claims 6 and 27.

The Applicant disagrees with the Examiner's objections, but for the sake of compact prosecution only, has amended claim 1 and submits that claims 1, 2, 6, 24 and 27 patentably distinguish the cited prior art.
Claim 1 (as amended) recites:
raster scanning the location of the focus point across a
body.h1: field of view in a vertical ... to provide a first xz plane
body.p: image;
scanning the location of the focus point in a y-direction
transverse to the vertical plane to obtain a sequence of
additional xz plane images ...;
wherein scanning the location of the focus point in the y
direction comprises holding the objective fixed in the y

p.u: direction while moving the tissue in the y direction.

body.p: (emphasis added)

The Examiner contends that Chen discloses y-direction scanning at sections 2.2-2.3 and Fig. 2.3. These aspects of Chen disclose x- and y-direction scanning using a resonant galvanometer scanner (resonant GS) in the x-direction and a regular galvanometer scanner (regular GS) in the y-direction. Both of these Chen techniques (resonant GS and regular GS) involve tilting mirrors. Chen fails to teach or suggest y-direction scanning that involves "holding the objective fixed in the y-direction while moving the tissue in the y-direction" as recited in claim 1.

Zeng fails to remedy this deficiency. In particular, Zeng discloses moving the objective to achieve y-direction scanning which contrasts directly with the claim 1 feature of "holding the objective fixed in the v-direction while moving the tissue in the v-direction". In particular, Figure 2B of Zeng (reproduced below) and paragraphs [0070] and [0071] of PGPub. 2014/0023993 describe a translation stage 156 comprising a plate 158 movably coupled to a base 160. Base 160 is fixed to an adapter 150 (paragraph [0071]) and adapter 150 is fixed to a patient's body with adhesive (paragraph [0070]). Objective 110 is securely mounted to plate 158 (paragraph [0071]). Zeng discloses that plate 158 (and therefore objective 110) move in XY directions relative to base 160 (and therefore adapter 150 and the patient's body).- see paragraph [0071].
1 Figure 2B

Accordingly, claim 1 (which recites) y-direction scanning that involves "holding the objective fixed in the y-direction while moving the tissue in the y-direction" directly contrasts with Zeng which discloses moving the objective relative to the patient's body.

This claim 1 feature of "holding the objective fixed in the y-direction while moving the tissue in the y-direction" advantageously achieves the technical effect of providing a significantly increased y-direction scanning range as compared to the Zeng technique of moving the objective. This increase in the y-direction scanning range results from the fact that the aperture of the objective is usually relatively small and, consequently, moving the objective in the y-direction (even by a small amount) in the manner taught by Zeng tends to move the objective aperture out of the fixed path of the incident beam. The y-direction scanning range is therefore limited by the objective aperture. In contrast, if the patient's tissue is moved to achieve y-direction scanning, the incident beam always impinges on the aperture of the objective.
Based on the reasoning presented above, the Applicant submits that claim 1 patentably distinguishes the cited references.
Claims 2, 6, 24 and 27 depend from claim 1 and are submitted to be patentable over the cited prior art for at least this reason.
The Examiner raised the combination of Chen and Zeng in relation to previously pending claims 32, 36 and 48.

The Applicant disagrees with the Examiner's objections, but for the sake of compact prosecution only, has amended claim 32 and submits that claims 32, 36 and 48 patentably distinguish the cited prior art.
Claim 32 (as amended) recites features analogous to those discussed above in relation to claim 1. In particular, claim 32 (as amended) recites:
a tissue stabilizing mechanism coupled to the objective
by way of a movable stage operative to move tissue relative to
the objective in a y direction that is transverse relative to
the x direction while holding the objective fixed,
a controller configured to generate ... control signals for
the movable stage to cause the focus point to be scanned in
the y direction,

As discussed above in relation to claim 1, the cited prior art fails to teach or suggest y- direction scanning that involves holding the objective fixed while moving the patient's tissue in the y-direction. Furthermore, this feature provides the technical advantage of a considerable increase in the range of y-direction scanning relative to the prior art.
Accordingly, the Applicant submits that claim 32 is patentable over the prior art of record.
Claims 36 and 48 depend from claim 32 and are submitted to be allowable for at least this reason.
